businessModel: Business model relevant to the forward-looking scenario
sourceNote: Blind-outcome case where the actual future outcome is hidden from the engine. Case presents a decision point where the owner must choose between strategic alternatives. Diagnosis should identify which alternative aligns with root-cause drivers and constraints. Actual outcome revealed only after diagnosis is complete (for oracle comparison). No answer-key content in inputs.

ownerIntake.businessType: Business description at the decision point (e.g., 'E-commerce platform for B2B beauty products, currently $3M ARR, 40% YoY growth, but facing margin compression and competitive pressure')
ownerIntake.stage: Stage with context for the decision (e.g., 'Series A candidate company with strong growth but profitability questions. Must choose strategic direction within 90 days')
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: The strategic goal, but decision point is ambiguous (e.g., 'Achieve sustainable unit economics and prepare for Series A, but unclear whether this requires geographic expansion, product consolidation, or go-to-market shift')
ownerConstraints: Constraint that bears on the strategic choice (e.g., 'Cannot raise capital until unit economics trajectory improves or clear path to profitability articulated')
Time constraint making the decision urgent (e.g., 'Must decide within 90 days; competitive window for expansion closing')
Resource constraint affecting which strategies are feasible (e.g., 'Engineering team fully allocated to core product; limited capacity for new market development or product expansion')
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: The strategic decision the owner faces (e.g., 'Should we expand into 3 new geographies to amortize product costs, consolidate into core market and optimize unit economics, or pivot to higher-margin enterprise segment?')
availableData: Current performance data: Current market performance, unit economics, customer cohort data, margin drivers
Strategic option analyses: Preliminary analysis of each strategic option (expansion, consolidation, pivot) with assumed outcomes
Market and competitive data: Market size, growth rates, competitive positioning, customer interviews
unavailableData: The outcome of the strategic choice (hidden from engine; will be revealed post-diagnosis)
Long-term customer cohort data for expansion markets (markets not yet entered)
Enterprise customer feedback (pivot not yet tested)
Execution risk details for each option (known to owner, not provided to engine)
ownerIntake.timeHorizon: 90 days (decision point, 12-month execution horizon if decision made)
ownerIntake.riskAppetite: MEDIUM (growth-dependent company balancing risk of capital constraint vs. execution risk of expansion)

clientContext.revenueImpactUrgency: CRITICAL (strategic choice directly determines capital availability and company direction)

businessProblem: Forward-looking decision scenario: 'A B2B beauty e-commerce platform has achieved rapid growth (40% YoY ARR growth to $3M) but faces a strategic fork. Unit economics are under pressure: gross margin declining from 48% (Year 1) to 41% (Year 2) due to customer acquisition costs rising faster than customer lifetime value. The owner has three strategic options: (1) Expand into 3 new geographies to amortize product/platform costs across larger customer base (high execution risk), (2) Consolidate to core market and optimize unit economics through retention and pricing (lower upside, faster profitability), (3) Pivot to higher-margin enterprise segment (unproven, requires product and sales shift). The company must decide within 90 days to secure capital for execution. Which strategy aligns with root-cause drivers of the margin compression, and which is most likely to succeed given the company's constraints and market realities?'

evidence.finding: Margin compression trend (e.g., 'Gross margin declined from 48% (Year 1) to 41% (Year 2), with COGS as % of revenue stable at 52%, indicating customer acquisition cost (CAC) inflation is primary driver')
evidence.source: Company financial statements, customer cohort analysis

evidence.finding: CAC inflation evidence (e.g., 'Blended CAC increased 35% from $180 (Year 1) to $243 (Year 2). Breakdown: core market CAC up 20% from $150 to $180 (saturation); secondary market CAC $320 (untested, high risk)')

Retention data by cohort (e.g., 'Year-1 cohorts (primary market): 24-month retention 52%. Year-2 cohorts (mixed primary/secondary): 12-month retention 48% (early data). Enterprise cohort (pilot): 12-month retention 78% with higher LTV')
evidence.confidence: MEDIUM (Year-2 data only 12-month, extrapolated to 24-month estimate lower)

evidence.finding: Competitive and market data (e.g., 'Core market growth 20% YoY, but company growing at 40% (market share gain). Secondary market competitors have 15-25% lower CAC due to lower brand awareness, suggesting either opportunity (expansion) or risk (commoditization). Enterprise segment: smaller market ($500M vs $2.5B core), but 2-3 year lag in digital adoption suggests opportunity window')
evidence.confidence: MEDIUM (market data from industry reports; company-specific competitive position less certain)
evidence.source: Industry analysis, competitive research, pilot feedback

strategicOptions.description: Expand into 3 new geographies to amortize product costs and achieve unit economics recovery
strategicOptions.rationale: If margin compression is driven by CAC inflation in saturated core market, geographic expansion into less-saturated markets may improve blended CAC and restore margins
strategicOptions.implementationRisk: HIGH (execution complexity, capital requirement $2-3M for go-to-market setup, uncertainty on secondary market performance)

strategicOptions.description: Consolidate to core market, focus on unit economics optimization through retention, pricing, and cost reduction
strategicOptions.rationale: If margin compression is driven by CAC inefficiency in core market, focused optimization may improve LTV:CAC ratio without expansion capital
strategicOptions.implementationRisk: MEDIUM (execution less complex, lower capital requirement ~$500k, but limits upside growth potential)

strategicOptions.description: Pivot to enterprise segment with customized product and higher-margin go-to-market
strategicOptions.rationale: Enterprise cohort shows 78% retention and higher LTV despite small sample; pivot could achieve superior unit economics if execution succeeds
strategicOptions.implementationRisk: HIGHEST (product pivot required, sales model transformation, uncertain market fit, capital requirement $1.5-2M, 12-18 month execution)
strategicOptions.timelineIfChosen: 12-18 months to first meaningful enterprise revenue

ownerConstraintProfile.budgetBand: LOW (bootstrapped; cannot support >$500k investment without capital raise)
ownerConstraintProfile.staffCapacity: LOW (founder + 3 full-time, limited bandwidth for major strategic shift)
